en.title: The best take on AI Native thinking I've heard this year—sincere and refreshingly down-to-earth.
en.summary: The author's notes distill Kuaishou's enterprise AI deployment experience into a practical playbook: first codify employee expertise into shared capabilities, then restructure how work is divided; use small teams to shorten delivery chains, pair that with an intelligent QA system that grades requirements by risk, and build a unified foundation plus a credit/points mechanism to control costs. This approach balances pilot experimentation with enterprise governance, helping teams of all sizes avoid Agent silos, idle spinning, and quality loss of control.
en.reason: Kuaishou’s Shen Lang maps enterprise AI productivity across four stages—R&D efficiency, more employees, team AI and organizational AI—and says AI Coding must next redesign software delivery, turn staff experience into shared assets and unify infrastructure.

en.title: After a year of tinkering, I'm open-sourcing my Agent automation system — I hope everyone gets to experience the magic of Agents.
en.summary: Kazik has open-sourced Agent-Autoloop after rebuilding the Agent automation system he uses himself. The architecture is plugin-based throughout: events, models, and notification channels can all be plugged in freely, and it works with most mainstream Agents. The article also showcases a large set of directly reusable automation scenarios, so individuals and teams can quickly build intelligent workflows that run autonomously and call for human approval on demand.
en.reason: Kazike open-sourced Agent-Autoloop, a year-long agent automation system rebuilt in two days drawing on Pi and DeepSeek Harness's plugin approach, making everything but the kernel a hot-swappable plugin for events, models and notifications, plus reusable approval workflows.

en.title: One person running a company with hundreds of AI Agents—this is what the independent developer workstation looks like now.
en.summary:
A single person running a company with hundreds of AI Agents — this is what the indie developer's desk looks like now.

Developer @EHuanglu's one-man battle log:
• Dozens of terminals packed across the screen, with hundreds of Agents running code, testing features, scraping data and handling operations in parallel in the background;
• The human doesn't write the grunt-work code, just sits at the top-level dashboard as CEO, reviewing summaries and clicking confirm;
• Software, hardware and phone monitoring all wired together — one person is a fully staffed digital outsourcing team.

Building a product used to mean hiring a group of people. Now it comes down to how many high-IQ agents one person can command at the same time.

📎 Video from @EHuanglu

#AIAgent #OnePersonCompany #SuperIndividual #IndieDev #AI

AI Is Running Faster and Faster—Who Holds the Emergency Stop?
You still hold control: the AI emergency stop is here—first, see what it can cut off. On November 3 at Fal.Con Europe in Barcelona, CrowdStrike put the AI emergency stop on the launch stage.
en.summary:
AI Is Running Faster and Faster. Who Holds the Emergency Stop?

“You Still Hold Control”: AI Kill Switch Goes Live—First, See What It Can Cut Off

On November 3 at Fal.Con Europe in Barcelona, CrowdStrike unveiled its AI kill switch. Founder and CEO George Kurtz said in the announcement that deploying agents with a kill switch means you still hold control. The scenario is easy to imagine: an agent with enterprise permissions keeps calling tools, then at some step suddenly deviates from the task. Admins need to hit stop before investigation can catch up. According to Security Boulevard that day, the new feature first blocks agents from accessing models through a connected AI gateway. CrowdStrike’s technical blog also lists broader controls, such as directly terminating endpoint processes and preventing restarts, as future extensions. That means, as you read…

en.title: The best take on AI Native thinking I've heard this year—sincere and refreshingly down-to-earth.
en.summary: The author's notes distill Kuaishou's enterprise AI deployment experience into a practical playbook: first codify employee expertise into shared capabilities, then restructure how work is divided; use small teams to shorten delivery chains, pair that with an intelligent QA system that grades requirements by risk, and build a unified foundation plus a credit/points mechanism to control costs. This approach balances pilot experimentation with enterprise governance, helping teams of all sizes avoid Agent silos, idle spinning, and quality loss of control.

en.title: One person running a company with hundreds of AI Agents—this is what the independent developer workstation looks like now.
en.summary:
A single person running a company with hundreds of AI Agents — this is what the indie developer's desk looks like now.

Developer @EHuanglu's one-man battle log:
• Dozens of terminals packed across the screen, with hundreds of Agents running code, testing features, scraping data and handling operations in parallel in the background;
• The human doesn't write the grunt-work code, just sits at the top-level dashboard as CEO, reviewing summaries and clicking confirm;
• Software, hardware and phone monitoring all wired together — one person is a fully staffed digital outsourcing team.

Building a product used to mean hiring a group of people. Now it comes down to how many high-IQ agents one person can command at the same time.

📎 Video from @EHuanglu

AI Is Running Faster and Faster. Who Holds the Emergency Stop?

“You Still Hold Control”: AI Kill Switch Goes Live—First, See What It Can Cut Off

On November 3 at Fal.Con Europe in Barcelona, CrowdStrike unveiled its AI kill switch. Founder and CEO George Kurtz said in the announcement that deploying agents with a kill switch means you still hold control. The scenario is easy to imagine: an agent with enterprise permissions keeps calling tools, then at some step suddenly deviates from the task. Admins need to hit stop before investigation can catch up. According to Security Boulevard that day, the new feature first blocks agents from accessing models through a connected AI gateway.
